assessment.nobel_worthiness: Condensate formation by liquid-liquid phase separation is a genuinely new organising principle for the cell, and it is physical chemistry at its core: demixing, interfacial tension, multivalency, viscoelasticity and phase diagrams applied to biomolecules. It reframed how compartmentalisation without membranes is understood and spread into neurodegeneration and cell biology.
assessment.attribution: The P-granule liquid-droplet work (Brangwynne, Hyman) and the multivalent signalling-protein phase transition (Rosen) are the clearest founding contributions; Pappu and Mittag supplied sequence-encoded physical grammar. A three-person prize is defensible but leaves out strong theory and sequence-grammar work.
assessment.maturity: More than a decade of replication and conceptual uptake, with active debate about which in vivo condensates are truly phase-separated and their functional relevance. Recognition is timely but the field is still sorting out rigour.
uncertainties: Controversy over whether many reported condensates are true equilibrium phase separation versus artefacts of overexpression
Fit with a chemistry rather than medicine or physiology prize
Fair allocation between experimental discoverers and theorists (Pappu, Mittag)

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a lipid self-assembly and pH-dependent phase-behaviour solution to nucleic-acid delivery, and they enabled the mRNA vaccines and siRNA therapeutics at global scale. The impact is immense and rests on real physical-chemical design of lipid structure, pKa and bilayer-to-nonbilayer transitions.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues established the ionizable-lipid LNP formulation concept and manufacturing; Anderson and Langer drove lipidoid and optimised ionizable-lipid libraries. Credit among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is tangled and I would need clearer evidence on which chemistry steps were decisive.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at enormous scale since 2018 (Onpattro) and 2020-21 (COVID-19 vaccines); well-confirmed and timely, although the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside modification already covered the mRNA side.
uncertainties: Messy allocation of credit among many LNP contributors and the role of patents and companies
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may make a chemistry award feel redundant to some
My recollection of who contributed which lipid design step is not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids via orthogonal tRNA-synthetase pairs and quadruplet and recoded codons rewrote the chemical alphabet of proteins in living cells. It is a conceptual and enabling advance for chemical biology, protein engineering and biophysical probing of membrane proteins and amyloid.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first orthogonal pair in E. coli and in eukaryotes; Chin extended to eukaryotes and animals, orthogonal ribosomes and genome recoding. Mehl and Yokoyama have important contributions too, so the three-person cut is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for over twenty years with many independent labs and clinical translation of non-natural amino acid-containing biologics; mature and stable.
uncertainties: Which of several close contributors (Mehl, Yokoyama) is left out
Possible perception that it is closer to molecular biology than chemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory and the folding funnel give a statistical-thermodynamic explanation of how proteins reach unique structures despite Levinthal's paradox, and unify theory with experimental phi-value analysis. It is the kind of general physical-chemical principle I value, linking thermodynamics and kinetics to biology.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes first formulated the funnel; Onuchic extended it and Wolynes with Onuchic developed the minimal frustration principle; Fersht established the experimental kinetic mapping of folding transition states. Dill's hydrophobic-collapse contributions arguably deserve equal weight, so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Decades old and conceptually absorbed into the field, though the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design partly addressed the folding problem; timing is not obviously fresh.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize on protein structure prediction and design
Credit split between theorists and experimentalist, and the omission of Dill
Whether the funnel picture still has testable predictive power relative to its textbook status

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another on DNA without double-strand breaks by fusing a deaminase to a Cas protein, an unquestionably chemistry-inflected genome-editing tool with rapid therapeutic translation and the first clinical successes.
assessment.attribution: Liu lab work is decisive, with Komor (cytosine) and Gaudelli (adenine) as lead first authors. A prize to Liu alone, possibly with prime editing (B057), is also plausible; CRISPR itself was already honoured in 2020.
assessment.maturity: Short time since 2016-2017, but strong independent replication, wide use and early clinical outcomes. Perhaps a few years early relative to the committee's usual lag.
uncertainties: Possible concern that it builds on CRISPR already honoured in 2020
Whether recognition should be bundled with prime editing and whether trainees should share credit
Long-term safety and off-target profiles still being established

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA and RNA molecules via ionic current through protein or solid-state nanopores is a clever union of molecular physics and chemistry, enabling long-read sequencing and single-molecule analysis of polymers and modifications.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz showed the concept; Bayley engineered protein pores and chemical detection; Akeson demonstrated enzyme ratcheting and base resolution. Branton's status and the precise decisive steps are uncertain to me, and a fair three-person split is hard.
assessment.maturity: Commercially mature and widely used for over a decade with strong independent confirmation; the maturity is high.
uncertainties: Possible deceased or unavailable candidates among the credited names which I cannot verify
Difficulty in apportioning credit between concept, pore engineering and enzyme ratchet
Whether sequencing falls nearer to a medicine or analytical-chemistry prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled thiol monolayers and soft lithography established molecularly defined surfaces and interfaces, central to colloid and surface chemistry, wetting, biointerfaces and microfabrication. A foundational, general concept in molecular organisation at interfaces.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara gave the early alkanethiol-on-gold monolayer; Whitesides developed the systematic SAM science and soft lithography; Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers complicate priority. The Nuzzo-Allara-Whitesides trio is reasonable but not clean.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of use; the risk is that it is now seen as long-established rather than newly decisive, and priority issues are unsettled.
uncertainties: Priority dispute with earlier silane monolayer work by Sagiv
Age and availability of the proposed laureates
Lack of a single stand-out discovery moment

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coordination-driven self-assembly of discrete cages and polyhedra from metals and ligands is a clean example of thermodynamic self-assembly yielding precisely defined molecular containers with host-guest, catalytic and stabilisation function.
assessment.attribution: Fujita's discrete cages and squares, Raymond's tetrahedral and related assemblies, and Stang's molecular polygons are the main lines. Nitschke and Ward are important successors; a three-person prize is fairly defensible.
assessment.maturity: Mature and well confirmed, but the 2025 prize on metal-organic frameworks makes the timing less favourable and may be perceived as covering similar ground.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 framework prize on coordination-driven assembly
Allocation among Fujita, Raymond and Stang plus later contributors
Limited practical impact compared to the other candidates
